native_result.query: How does incarceration affect the wealth of black individuals based on their income levels?
native_result.HypoA: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
native_result.HypoB: Among black NLSY79 respondents, incarceration (ever jailed 1985-1994) is associated with lower subsequent wealth and smaller 1985-1996 wealth accumulation, and this association is strongest for those with higher baseline (1985) wealth/economic standing. The mean 1985-to-1996 wealth shortfall of the jailed vs non-jailed group rises monotonically across 1985-wealth tertiles: low tier ~$17.5k (jail n=76), mid tier ~$29.4k (jail n=39), high tier ~$59.0k (jail n=44); in the high-wealth tier the jailed group shows a mean NEGATIVE 1985-1996 change (~-$4.2k) while non-jailed gain ~+$54.8k. This is a descriptive association, not a causal estimate: the jailed group is heavily male (83-98%) and starts from lower baseline wealth, so selection/confounding cannot be ruled out.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, 6 cols, 0 missing). Confirmed NO income/income-bracket/asset-income field exists. 2) Restricted to race=='black' (n=3,013; ever_jailed=159, 5.3%). 3) Used composite_wealth_1985 as the pre-incarceration proxy for income/economic level and stratified into tertiles (q33=0, q67=3830 -> low/mid/high); verified jailed sub-cells all >=15 (76/39/44) so 3 tiers retained. 4) Computed wealth changes d96=w1996-w1985 (primary, post-window) and d90=w1990-w1985 (aux, mid-window), plus 1996 level. 5) Within each tier compared ever_jailed=1 vs 0 on mean and median, reporting n and using sex as the only simple control; computed the not-jailed-minus-jailed gap. 6) Reported a monotonic pattern: the incarceration-associated wealth shortfall grows with baseline wealth tier. All figures reproducible via analysis.py; summary in results_summary.txt.

sub_hypo.text: Among black NLSY79 respondents, being jailed during 1985–1994 is associated with lower 1996 wealth and smaller 1985–1996 wealth accumulation.
sub_hypo.context: Black NLSY79 respondents (n=3,013; 159 ever jailed), compared within baseline 1985 wealth tertiles defined using cut points of 0 and 3,830.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed versus non-jailed respondents are compared on mean and median 1996 wealth and 1996-minus-1985 wealth change, with sex as the only simple control. Incarceration is descriptively associated with lower subsequent wealth and smaller wealth accumulation, not established as a causal effect.

sub_hypo.text: The incarceration-associated 1985–1996 mean wealth accumulation shortfall increases monotonically with baseline wealth: approximately $17.5k in the low tertile, $29.4k in the middle tertile, and $59.0k in the high tertile.
sub_hypo.context: Black NLSY79 respondents stratified by 1985 wealth tertiles using cut points of 0 and 3,830; jailed counts are 76, 39, and 44 in the low, middle, and high tiers, respectively. Baseline wealth proxies economic standing because no income field exists.
sub_hypo.relations: The non-jailed-minus-jailed gap in mean 1996-minus-1985 wealth change rises monotonically across baseline wealth tertiles, indicating the strongest negative incarceration association at higher baseline economic standing.

sub_hypo.text: Within the high baseline wealth tertile, jailed black respondents lose approximately $4.2k in mean wealth between 1985 and 1996, while non-jailed respondents gain approximately $54.8k.
sub_hypo.context: Black NLSY79 respondents in the high 1985 wealth tertile; 44 respondents were jailed during 1985–1994.
sub_hypo.relations: Mean 1996-minus-1985 wealth change is negative for jailed respondents and positive for non-jailed respondents, producing an approximately $59.0k accumulation gap.

sub_hypo.text: The jailed group is heavily male and starts with lower baseline wealth, so selection and confounding cannot be ruled out.
sub_hypo.context: Black NLSY79 respondents compared by incarceration status within 1985 wealth tertiles; sex is the only simple control.
